One missing point added.
Would it make sense to create some sort of warning if `$NUM_COMMITS > 1`? I'm not sure if we would want to fail in that case, but we might be able to add a note to the MR.

Which warning do you have in mind? There is the echo of how many commits (very hard to find in the logs). As far as I know gitlab doesn't provide better notifications. We could add new stage that fails if num_commits > 1, but with allow_failure: true. That would be visible in the main pipeline page. That would not stop the MR to go ahead but would give a strong feedback that can be used by reviewers.

Also, we could use alpine image that gitlab points as the smallest linux image (for faster boot).
Can we merge this as is, or more work needed?

added 3596 commits
  • 5708937b...318bbfce - 3595 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • 4904d576 - ci: run checks on all the commits in the current MR.
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/1480/diffs?diff_id=302758398&start_sha=5708937b6294ea2e138f39d7b750b1945faad30a)

I've rebased the MR against the current master. There was a note from @geraldcombs about adding a note, but:

- we cannot make the CI fail in case NUM_COMMITS are > 1
- A "note" (like echo) will get unnoticed
- I may have missed a smarter way to "annotate" something: if so, please let me know, otherwise we can't do that.

I was thinking that we could post a message to the MR using the GitLab API using CI_JOB_TOKEN, but that doesn't seem to have [sufficient permissions](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/jobs/ci_job_token.html). I'm OK with the change going in in its current state until we can setup a "post messages" access token.

> I was thinking that we could post a message to the MR using the GitLab API using CI_JOB_TOKEN, but that doesn't seem to have [sufficient permissions](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/ci/jobs/ci_job_token.html).

According to [documentation](https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/api/notes.html#create-new-merge-request-note) a PRIVATE-TOKEN is required. AFAIK, setting one valid token (as of @ws-gitlab-utility's) should suffice, but I'm not aware of limits in forks interactions.

BTW, I'm moving this forward, since it's not blocking for future developments.
